challenges_to_claims.issue: The claim reports 48842 source rows next to a training positive rate without stating the training row count or split method. The profiles imply about 3200 training rows, so the claim may mislead about the data actually analyzed. The empty limitations list is not justified.

'0 features triggered' covers only 10 of 14 features, because feature_profiles lacks 4. Zero missingness is potentially an artifact of factorization. PSI is null for sex. The near-unique fnlwgt is not flagged and thresholds are not shown. The conclusion of no risk is not supported, and the claim's kind ('risk') conflicts with its content, which asserts absence of risk.

decision: Treat C1 as a descriptive fact with an undisclosed-split caveat. Treat C2 as unsupported or incomplete. Do not approve any feature and do not proceed to modeling until the profiling is completed on raw categories for all 14 features and a decision-time/production-availability review is done.

next_experiment.hypothesis: After restoring raw categorical values and profiling all 14 features on the documented split, at least one feature will be flagged for hidden missingness (raw missing tokens or sentinel codes), identifier-like behavior (fnlwgt), or redundancy (education vs education-num) that the cached-matrix profile missed. If none is flagged, the current C2 conclusion is corroborated.
next_experiment.success_gate: Pass only if all of the following hold: (1) the profile covers 14/14 features with non-null PSI or an explicit documented reason for null; (2) raw missing-token counts are reported per categorical feature and reconciled with the cached missing_rate values; (3) train/holdout row counts and split method are reported and reconcile with the 48842 source rows; (4) review-rule thresholds are published and re-applied; (5) every feature has a documented decision-time and production-availability verdict, with unreviewed features marked 'not approved'. Failing any item keeps the modeling block in place.
next_experiment.title: Raw-category, full-coverage data audit with decision-time availability table
next_experiment.why_smallest: It is a descriptive audit only. It trains no model and spends no modeling budget; it just closes the profile-coverage, missingness-masking and availability gaps that block every later experiment.

risks_and_missing_evidence: Profile coverage gap: 10 of 14 features are profiled, so the 'zero flagged' statement cannot be verified for the remaining 4.
Training size and split method (random, stratified, seed) are not reported; the profiles appear to cover about 3200 rows rather than 48842 (inference from unique_count/unique_ratio).
Missingness may be masked by factorization: all missing rates are 0.0 and the categoricals are float64. Raw missing tokens and sentinel codes need to be restored and counted.
random_split_psi is null for sex with no reason given, which suggests the metric silently fails for some features.
fnlwgt is nearly unique per row and is not flagged. Review rule thresholds are not disclosed, and whether it is available at decision time is unreviewed.
education and education-num look redundant (same cardinality and top-value frequency). This duplication was not checked.
Sensitive or protected attributes (sex, race, marital-status, relationship) have had no production-availability, legal or fairness review.
Target definition and label timing are not documented. There is no leakage review for any feature (decision-time availability, proxies for the label).
Duplicate-row and train/test contamination checks are absent. The 48842 source rows may merge the original UCI train and test partitions, and the provenance is unstated.
Random-split PSI cannot speak to temporal or population stability, as the claim's own limitation states.
Only the training positive rate is given; the holdout rate and the source-wide positive rate are missing.

challenges_to_claims.issue: The fact itself is supported, but it should not be read as evidence that real columns are leak-free. Only exact-target detection was tested, with no partial-proxy canary and no reported detector settings.

'Declared exclusions: none' is a decision claim backed by an empty list and a null CV result. It lacks any per-column review or decision-time/availability documentation, and its cited evidence (safe_vs_unsafe_training_cv) is empty. It may be misread as 'no leakage found', which the bundle does not support.

decision: Do not accept 'no exclusions' as a cleared leakage audit. Treat the audit as incomplete and all adult columns as unreviewed for decision-time and production availability. No feature is approved. C1 can be kept as a narrow detector-sanity fact; C2 should be held pending evidence.

next_experiment.hypothesis: If adult columns are all available at the prediction time and none are target proxies, then (a) no column will exceed the pre-registered univariate AUC and uniqueness review thresholds without a documented availability justification, (b) a noisy partial-proxy canary (e.g., target copy with ~20% label flips) will be flagged by the detector, and (c) the grouped-CV score of the full feature set will not differ from the score of a set excluding any flagged columns beyond fold-to-fold variability.
next_experiment.success_gate: Pre-register the thresholds and the prediction-time contract before running. The gate passes only if all hold: (1) every column has a recorded decision-time and production-availability annotation with its source; (2) the detector flags the noisy partial-proxy canary; (3) safe_vs_unsafe_training_cv is non-null with fold-level scores and variability; (4) every column flagged by the name, AUC, or uniqueness rules has a documented human disposition (keep with justification, or exclude). Failure of (2) means the detector is insufficient for proxy detection. Any flagged column whose removal changes CV beyond the fold standard deviation must be escalated for review. This is a predictive comparison only and implies no causal effect.
next_experiment.title: Per-column decision-time review plus partial-proxy canary and populated safe-vs-unsafe CV on adult
next_experiment.why_smallest: It reuses the existing detector and dataset, adds one more canary, fills the missing CV field, and produces the per-column table that the current bundle lacks, without adding new models or features.

risks_and_missing_evidence: No per-column leakage diagnostics (univariate AUC, cardinality/uniqueness, name-pattern flags) are reported, so suspicious proxies cannot be identified or ruled out.
No decision-time or production-availability review is documented for any column; only such semantics can confirm or refute leakage.
safe_vs_unsafe_training_cv is null, so the effect of removing or retaining candidate columns on validation performance is unknown (and it is unclear whether the step was skipped or failed).

A canary pass shows detector sensitivity only for an exact-target copy. It does not show sensitivity to partial proxies, noisy transforms, or combinations of columns, and says nothing about specificity or false-negative rate on real data.

Adult has known semantic risks that were not examined in this bundle, for example redundant encodings (education vs education-num) and sensitive or protected attributes. Whether any column is proxy-like or unavailable at prediction time depends on the intended use, which is unspecified, so this is a hypothesis to review and not a finding.
The prediction-time contract (the decision moment and the intended deployment use) is not stated in the bundle, so 'violation' cannot be assessed.
Validation design is not described (split strategy, duplicates across folds, preprocessing fit inside folds), so train/test or preprocessing leakage cannot be excluded.
The bundle is internally inconsistent: C2 cites safe_vs_unsafe_training_cv as evidence but its value is null, and the top-level limitations are empty despite the C2 limitation.

challenges_to_claims.issue: The recommendation is a screening choice, but it implicitly endorses 14 raw features with no decision-time or production-availability review. fnlwgt, the most important raw feature, is a sampling weight, and four sensitive demographic attributes are included.

The choice of raw over interactions rests on a 0.00012 ROC-AUC gap judged by an arbitrary 0.002 tolerance, against a fold std of about 0.0065 with 3 folds, 1 repeat and overlapping CIs. The evidence cannot distinguish raw from interactions, ratios or full_fe.

The research question concerns validation evidence and feature dilution, but only training-CV is reported, with no held-out validation and no controlled dilution test. Stages are cumulative, so no stage-level result isolates feature count or any single feature family.

The claim does not mention that the selected stage (25 features, ROC-AUC 0.8862) is the worst stage, nor that its selection procedure and fold-internal fitting are undocumented. The 'train-fitted' premise is therefore unverified.

The limitations field in the evidence bundle is empty and the claim limitation is generic. The missing items are the non-domain transforms on categorical codes, the truncated stability tables, the single metric and fixed threshold, and the undisclosed fold sizes.

decision: Provisional only. Raw can be carried into the next model screen as a baseline under the declared selection rule, but EXP-003-C1 should not be read as evidence that feature engineering does not help, nor as production approval of any raw feature. The raw recipe should not be approved for use until decision-time and production-availability review has covered fnlwgt, the sensitive attributes (sex, race, marital-status, native-country) and the other raw columns. Re-run with repeated paired CV and confirm on an untouched hold-out before any stronger claim.

next_experiment.hypothesis: Under paired repeated stratified CV, interactions-stage ROC-AUC does not differ from raw by more than 0.002, and dropping fnlwgt from raw changes ROC-AUC by no more than 0.002. Falsified if either difference exceeds 0.002 beyond its CI.
next_experiment.success_gate: Run at least 5 repeats x 3 folds (15 paired evaluations) with fixed seeds and all encoders, k-means and selection fitted inside each training fold. Raw is retained as the next-screen baseline only if the 95% CI of the paired difference (interactions minus raw) lies within [-0.002, +0.002]. If the lower CI bound is above 0.002, interactions is advanced instead. If raw-without-fnlwgt is more than 0.002 below raw in mean paired ROC-AUC, fnlwgt dependence is recorded as a blocking availability-review item. Report log_loss, Brier and ECE alongside ROC-AUC, and report fold sizes and class prevalence. No feature is approved from this run without a documented decision-time and production-availability review.
next_experiment.title: Paired repeated-CV re-test of raw vs interactions vs raw-without-fnlwgt on identical folds
next_experiment.why_smallest: It reuses the existing LightGBM baseline and the cheapest stages (each stage took about 0.4-0.7 s) and changes only the CV protocol and one feature-drop arm. It targets the two main weaknesses: noise in the ranking and dependence on fnlwgt. It requires no new feature families, tuning or model changes.

risks_and_missing_evidence: No held-out validation set is reported. All numbers are 3-fold, 1-repeat training-CV, even though the question asks about validation evidence. Fold sizes and class prevalence are not reported. The recall values imply only a few hundred positives per fold, which is an inference to be confirmed.

No decision-time or production-availability review is documented for any feature. fnlwgt is a census sampling weight, not an individual attribute, and it is the top raw feature and the base of the top engineered ratios, so its availability at decision time is doubtful. Sex, race, marital-status and native-country are sensitive attributes needing legal and fairness review. education and education-num are likely redundant.

Generic transforms were applied to apparently categorical columns, e.g. log1p_education, log1p_marital-status, ratio_fnlwgt_div_native-country. These imply ordinal-coded categoricals with no domain meaning. This is inferred from feature names, since the encoding is not shown.

The evidence does not show that encoders, k-means (kmeans_cluster), interaction construction and feature selection were fitted inside each training fold. The 'train-fitted' premise is asserted but not demonstrated, so fold-level leakage cannot be excluded.
The stages are cumulative, with no per-family ablation. The interactions-stage gain (+0.00012) cannot be attributed to any family, and the selected stage's procedure is undocumented.
The 0.002 tolerance is arbitrary and about 3x smaller than the fold std (0.0065). The rule is not calibrated against noise, and the ROC-AUC choice may flip with a different seed or fold split.

Selection used a single metric (ROC-AUC). Other metrics disagree on ranking (accuracy, F1 and precision favor interactions; log_loss favors raw), and the fixed 0.5 threshold is not tuned or justified.
The same fold-level metrics for raw and logs suggest zero-importance additions. The feature_stability tables are truncated to 20 rows, so full feature sets cannot be audited.
Importance values are normalized model-internal scores and must not be read as causal or monotonic effects. The importance of fnlwgt-derived features may reflect sampling artifacts.

challenges_to_claims.issue: The LightGBM lead over HistGradientBoosting (about 0.0002 mean ROC-AUC, inconsistent per-fold sign) is within fold noise from 3 folds and 1 repeat. Naming a single candidate overstates the evidence, and HistGradientBoosting is effectively tied.
The question asks for 'strongest stable' evidence, but stability rests on a 3-fold std. HistGradientBoosting and LightGBM stds differ by only about 0.0025 and are themselves unreliable estimates.

The ranking uses ROC-AUC alone. ExtraTrees has better log loss and Brier, and logistic regression has much better ECE, so 'best' is metric-dependent. If probabilities will be used, calibration matters.
The claim says 'raw features' without any decision-time or production-availability review. LightGBM leans heavily on fnlwgt, and sex and race are included, so the candidate is not feature-approved.
Baseline-only models (no tuning) cannot support a conclusion about algorithm family strength, only about default configurations.

decision: Keep LightGBM as a provisional training-CV candidate, tied with HistGradientBoosting, pending repeated paired CV. Do not call it the strongest or a stable winner. Make no deployment claim and do not touch the locked holdout. Do not approve any feature (including fnlwgt, sex, race, native-country) without decision-time and production-availability review.

next_experiment.hypothesis: If LightGBM is genuinely better than HistGradientBoosting on raw features, its paired ROC-AUC advantage will be positive and consistent across 5x repeated stratified 5-fold CV on identical, de-duplicated splits. If the two are tied, the paired difference interval will include zero.
next_experiment.success_gate: LightGBM is retained as sole candidate only if (a) the mean paired ROC-AUC difference (LightGBM minus HistGradientBoosting) over the 25 folds is > 0, (b) the 95% interval for that difference, computed over per-repeat means to respect dependence, excludes 0, and (c) LightGBM wins in at least 70% of folds. Otherwise declare a tie and break it using log loss, ECE and runtime. Report fnlwgt-in and fnlwgt-out ROC-AUC as a sensitivity check without approving either.
next_experiment.title: Paired repeated stratified CV: LightGBM vs HistGradientBoosting on identical splits (training data only)
next_experiment.why_smallest: It changes only the evaluation protocol (more repeats, shared splits, de-duplication) for the two leading models. It adds no new models, tuning or features, directly tests whether the observed gap is noise, and does not touch the holdout.

risks_and_missing_evidence: Only 3 folds and 1 repeat, so fold std and CI95 are very noisy. The 0.25×std penalty is not a reliable stability measure, and the ranking margin is within noise.
All models are untuned baselines. Tuning budgets and defaults differ across families, so the result may reflect default hyperparameters rather than algorithm family strength.
Preprocessing is not documented. Encoders, imputation, and category handling must be fit inside the training folds, and the handling of categoricals differs across the compared models.
Split design is not reported: stratification, grouping, and duplicate-row handling. Duplicate rows are common in Adult-style data and can inflate CV if split across folds.
The dataset size is not given, so the sample behind the folds is unknown.
fnlwgt is a census sampling weight. Its decision-time meaning and production availability are unreviewed, and its high LightGBM importance is a risk flag, not a finding.
Sex, race, native-country and marital-status/relationship are included as raw features. There is no fairness or legal and production-availability review, and no subgroup metrics are reported.

The default 0.5 threshold is used for accuracy, F1, precision and recall. These are not comparable across models with different calibration, and ECE is notably worse for boosted models (about 0.058-0.067) than for logistic regression (0.0195).
The empty feature_stability for HistGradientBoosting prevents comparing the top-two models' feature reliance.
Importance values are model-specific and split-based for LightGBM, with different scales across families. They are not comparable and not causal.
No holdout evidence, as the claim itself notes. The bundle's limitations list is empty, which understates the claim-level limitations.

challenges_to_claims.issue: The claim is factually supported as a holdout score, but it does not address the question's optimization-gain component. It omits CV baseline vs tuned results, and the empty limitations hide that the CI is bootstrap-over-test-set only and that the holdout size is unreported.
The phrase 'preselected recipe' is not backed by evidence showing the selection-rule outcome (tuned vs baseline) or a CV delta against the 0.001 gate.

As a recommendation it is appropriate, but the cited evidence contains no decision-time or production-availability assessment. It is also based on 3 folds and an unspecified importance type, and fnlwgt (top feature) and the sensitive attributes are not flagged. The empty limitations field is inadequate.
Top importance and fold-stability are descriptive predictive-model statistics. They must not be read as evidence that any feature has a causal effect or is suitable for production.

decision: Accept EXP-005-C1 only as a narrow descriptive fact about holdout performance of the preselected recipe. Do not accept any claim that optimization helped, because the CV comparison is absent. Treat EXP-005-C2 as a sound process recommendation. It does not approve any feature, and fnlwgt, sex, race and native-country need explicit decision-time, production-availability and governance review. The holdout is consumed, so no further model or recipe choices may be informed by it. No deployment approval is implied.

next_experiment.hypothesis: Mean ROC-AUC of lightgbm_C02 exceeds the baseline by at least 0.001 in paired repeated stratified CV on the training split, and the paired-difference interval excludes zero. If not, the optimization gain is not distinguishable from noise.
next_experiment.success_gate: Using identical folds (e.g. 5 folds x 5 repeats, fixed seeds) on the training split only, report the per-fold paired ROC-AUC difference (C02 minus baseline). Pass if mean difference >= 0.001 and the 95% paired-bootstrap or t-interval lower bound is > 0. Otherwise the baseline is preferred, per the stated selection rule. The holdout is not touched. Also record the ROC-AUC change when fnlwgt is dropped, as a descriptive diagnostic only.
next_experiment.title: Paired repeated-CV comparison of baseline vs lightgbm_C02 on training data only, with fnlwgt-ablation as a secondary reading
next_experiment.why_smallest: It reuses the existing candidates and selection rule, needs no new tuning and no holdout access, and directly supplies the missing CV-gain evidence with a variance estimate.

risks_and_missing_evidence: No CV scores (per-fold or mean) are given for the baseline or tuned candidates, and the selected recipe is not identified as tuned or baseline. The optimization-gain question cannot be evaluated (evidence.selection_rule is a rule only).
No holdout comparison against the baseline is given, so it is unknown whether any difference exists at all. Any future baseline-vs-tuned comparison on this holdout would be a second use of it.
The bootstrap CI reflects test-sample variance only. Seed, training-split and tuning variance are not captured, and the holdout sample size and positive count are not reported.
The 0.001 improvement gate is small and its noise floor is unknown. With only 3 CV folds, a gain of that size may be indistinguishable from fold variance.

Importance type and method are unspecified. Impurity or split-count importance is biased, is not a measure of predictive contribution, and implies no causal effect. Permutation or ablation on validation folds is absent.

fnlwgt is a survey sampling weight, so its decision-time meaning and production availability are doubtful. Its dominant importance warrants a leakage/artifact review (for example, ordering or sampling-design effects).
sex, race and native-country are protected or sensitive attributes. No fairness, legal or policy review is shown, and importance rankings say nothing about their permissibility.
education and education-num are likely redundant, so importance may be split or unstable between them.
A single 0.5 threshold is reported with no cost or prevalence rationale. Precision and recall may shift materially with a different operating point.
Preprocessing and fit-in-fold hygiene (encoders, imputers fit on training folds only) is not documented, and dataset duplicates or split-level leakage checks are not shown.
The empty limitations fields overstate certainty, since the gaps above exist.

challenges_to_claims.issue: States that 0 features triggered review rules, but profiles for only 9 of 16 features are present in evidence.feature_profiles. The claim is unsupported for the remaining 7.

Empty production_risks lists are not evidence of production readiness. The rules checked cover only missingness, identifiers, near-constant values, and random-split shift. No decision-time availability or leakage rule was evaluated, and PSI is null for default, housing, and loan.

Mixes the 45211 source-row count with a training positive rate that appears to come from a smaller sample (about 3200 rows implied by unique_ratio). Population and split are unstated, and limitations are empty.
missing_rate 0.0 on float64 factorized categoricals may reflect the encoding rather than true completeness. 'Unknown' levels and sentinel codes are not examined.
day_of_week with 31 unique values contradicts its name, suggesting a mislabeled field and unreliable metadata.

decision: Hold modeling. Do not accept C2 as written. Complete the full 16-feature profile on the stated data population, restore raw category semantics, and run an explicit decision-time and production-availability review for every feature before any model is fit.

next_experiment.hypothesis: After restoring raw categories and profiling all 16 features on the full 45211-row source (with the train split size stated), at least one feature will be flagged for unavailability at decision time or for sentinel/unknown handling, and the sample-size discrepancy will be explained. If no flag appears and the discrepancy is trivially explained, the current 'no risks' reading is supported.
next_experiment.success_gate: Pass only if all of the following hold. (1) 16 profiles are emitted, one per feature, with raw dtype and category labels. (2) Profile n and train/holdout n reconcile with source_rows 45211 and are reported. (3) Every feature has a recorded decision-time availability status (available, unavailable, or unknown) with a named reviewer. (4) PSI is non-null for all features, including default, housing, and loan, using a categorical PSI. (5) A time-ordered split PSI is reported alongside the random-split PSI. (6) The meaning of day_of_week is documented. Fail if any feature has an unknown availability status or if the n discrepancy is unexplained; modeling stays blocked in that case.
next_experiment.title: Full 16-feature data audit with raw categories and decision-time availability table
next_experiment.why_smallest: It is a metadata and profiling pass using existing data, with no model fitting. It directly closes the verifiable gaps in C1 and C2: coverage, population, category semantics, availability, and temporal shift.

risks_and_missing_evidence: Profile coverage gap: 9 of 16 features are shown (EXP-006 / evidence.feature_profiles vs evidence.feature_count). Features not shown may include call-outcome or campaign-history fields whose availability at decision time is unreviewed.

Population mismatch (inferred): the implied profile n is about 3200, versus source_rows 45211. Whether the profiles and the positive rate describe a subsample or the full train split is not documented, and the split protocol and train/holdout sizes are absent.

Possible post-decision (leakage) features: a call-outcome or call-duration style field, if present among the unshown 7 features, would not be known before the contact decision. This cannot be verified from the evidence, so no feature can be approved.
day_of_week has 31 unique integer values, so it is likely day-of-month or mislabeled. Its semantics need confirmation, and any month or date field needed for a temporal split must be identified.

Factorized categoricals: the codes are ordinal artifacts, 'unknown' levels may be coded as ordinary categories or sentinels, and the missing_rate of 0.0 is not meaningful until raw categories are restored. The encoders must also handle unseen categories in production.
PSI is null for three binary features, so the shift check is incomplete for them. Random-split PSI is only a smoke test and says nothing about temporal drift.
A single positive-rate figure from training says nothing about stability across time or segments, or about the holdout rate.
Empty limitations on C1 and on the bundle overstate certainty.

challenges_to_claims.issue: The canary pass is true as stated, but it is easily over-read. It validates the detector only against an exact-target copy and carries no limitations. It does not show the detector would flag partial proxies, post-outcome fields, or time-shifted features among the real columns.

The +0.1842 AUC lift is reported as an apparent training-CV effect, which is fine. But the exclusion of 'duration' is a declaration without recorded decision-time evidence (such as a data dictionary or event timestamp). The claim also does not show that other columns were examined, so it should not be read as an answer to 'which columns violate the contract'. The lift reflects predictive association only, not causation.

The effective sample for the AUC comparison is 3 folds with 1 repeat. The statement gives a point estimate without the CI, and the safe and unsafe CIs, while non-overlapping, are not paired or repeated.

decision: Keep 'duration' excluded from any prediction-time model pending confirmation of its decision-time semantics. Do not treat the 15-feature set as cleared or approve any feature: no decision-time or production-availability review for the remaining columns is documented in the evidence. Treat EXP-007 as a partial audit: it supports the 'duration' exclusion but does not answer the full question.

next_experiment.hypothesis: No retained column in the 15-feature safe set is a hidden decision-time violation or near-target proxy. Specifically, each has a documented availability at prediction time, and none shows a single-column AUC or drop-column effect that is an outlier. This is falsified if any retained column lacks a confirmed pre-decision timestamp or fails the quantitative gate.
next_experiment.success_gate: Pre-registered before running: (1) 16 of 16 columns have a documented availability status (available at decision time / not available / unknown) confirmed by the data owner, with zero 'unknown' for the columns kept; (2) the detector outputs name, univariate AUC, and uniqueness flags for every column; (3) using identical stratified folds with at least 5 repeats, no retained column has a univariate AUC above 0.80 or a leave-one-feature-out safe-model AUC drop above 0.05 without a documented availability justification; (4) the split strategy (stratified, entity-grouped, or time-ordered) is recorded. Fail if any column is unknown or breaches (3). Thresholds are proposed here and are not observed values.
next_experiment.title: Full-column availability audit plus drop-one-group ablation on the safe set with fixed repeated folds
next_experiment.why_smallest: It reuses the existing LightGBM baseline and fold framework, changes only the features (drop one at a time), and adds a documentation step. It needs no new modeling, tuning, or models, and it directly targets the unanswered part of the question.

risks_and_missing_evidence: Missing: per-column detector output (name-pattern, univariate AUC, uniqueness/cardinality flags) for all 16 columns. Only the declared feature and a canary are reported, so the claim of a complete audit is unsupported.

Missing: a decision-time and production-availability table for the 15 retained columns. Candidates needing timing review are month, day_of_week, contact, pdays, previous and poutcome. month and day_of_week carry high importance, and their meaning relative to prediction time is not documented.

The canary tests only an exact-target copy. It gives no evidence of recall for noisy, partial, or temporally leaked proxies, so a passing canary should not be read as a clean bill for the other columns.

Validation is thin: 3 folds, 1 repeat, a single default-parameter model, and default thresholds. The CI half-widths are not negligible relative to the safe-model AUC. No split strategy (stratification, grouping by customer/entity, or time-ordering) is stated, so duplicate-entity or temporal leakage across folds cannot be ruled out.

Feature importance is a model-specific, within-fit diagnostic. It does not establish proxy behavior or the absence of leakage, and it is unstable with correlated features. Equal importance ranks between safe and unsafe models do not clear any column.
The 'apparent' lift comes from training-CV only. There is no holdout or time-based evaluation to check whether the safe-set AUC is itself inflated by an unreviewed column.

Claim C2 is typed 'decision' but mixes a declaration with a metric. Its stated limitation (only decision-time semantics can confirm leakage) means the exclusion rests on out-of-band semantic knowledge that is not recorded in the bundle. The bundle-level limitations list is empty despite these gaps.
Dataset size, class balance, and the positive rate are not in the evidence, so the precision/recall figures and the AUC CIs cannot be put in context.

challenges_to_claims.issue: The claim says ratios 'achieved 0.7172' but does not state that the gain over raw (0.7130) is only about +0.0042, versus a fold std of about 0.013-0.017. The claim also has no paired or repeated comparison.

The claim implies improvement 'without feature dilution' but cites only ROC-AUC. Ratios adds 23 features, worsens log_loss, Brier and ECE, and shrinks the importance of the strongest raw features. Dilution is not tested.

The stated limitation covers domain meaning only. It omits that ratios appear to use categorical-coded columns and that decision-time availability has not been reviewed. A recommendation to use these features needs that review first.
The selected stage (25 features, ROC-AUC 0.7029) is undocumented and conflicts with the selection rule's apparent outcome. The claim is silent on this inconsistency.
The CV scores are used both to choose the recipe and to report its performance, which allows selection bias. The claim should be labeled as exploratory training-CV evidence.

decision: Do not accept EXP-008-C1 as an evidence-supported improvement. At most, carry ratios forward as a provisional, non-approved candidate arm alongside the raw baseline, pending a repeated paired comparison. No feature is approved for production without decision-time availability and production-semantics review.

next_experiment.hypothesis: If the ratios gain is real and not noise or a categorical-code artifact, ratios (and numeric-only ratios, built from true numeric columns only: age, balance, campaign, pdays, previous) will beat raw on paired ROC-AUC across repeated stratified folds, without log_loss degradation beyond a small margin.
next_experiment.success_gate: Using 5 repeats of stratified 5-fold CV with identical seeds and folds across arms, and all feature generation fit inside each training fold, the candidate must meet both conditions. (1) The paired mean ROC-AUC delta vs raw is at least +0.003, and the lower bound of a paired 95% interval (bootstrap over fold deltas) is above 0. (2) The mean log_loss is not more than 0.005 worse than raw. The candidate must also beat raw in at least 70% of folds. If ratios fails, or only numeric-only ratios passes, the ratios claim is falsified in its current form. Any arm that passes remains unapproved until the decision-time availability review is done.
next_experiment.title: Paired repeated-CV comparison of raw vs ratios vs numeric-only ratios under identical in-fold fitting
next_experiment.why_smallest: It keeps the model, params and metrics fixed and changes only fold count/repeats and one ablation arm. It directly tests the noise and categorical-encoding explanations without new feature families, tuning, or a new dataset.

risks_and_missing_evidence: Only 3 folds and 1 repeat are used, with no paired statistical comparison. Per-fold deltas change sign, and the ROC-AUC ci95 intervals overlap (evidence.stage_results[2].metrics.roc_auc vs evidence.stage_results[0].metrics.roc_auc).

The evidence is training-CV only. The stage choice and the 0.002 tolerance are tuned on the same CV scores that are reported, so the 0.7172 is optimistically biased. There is no untouched holdout or temporal split. If the data has time order (month, day_of_week, pdays), random CV may be inappropriate.

Nothing documents that feature generation, encoding, and any importance-based selection were fit inside each training fold. Varying observed_folds for ratio features suggests the feature set differs by fold, so 'the ratios recipe' is not one fixed feature matrix. The reported 'about 38' is a mean.

It is not documented how categorical columns (job, month, day_of_week, education, marital) were encoded before ratio, log1p and interaction generation. Ratios such as age/day_of_week or balance/job are not interpretable if the codes are arbitrary.

Decision-time and production availability are not reviewed for any feature: pdays, previous, poutcome, contact, campaign, month, day_of_week. No feature provenance or leakage audit is included. A leakage audit should also confirm that no post-outcome variable such as call duration is present. It is absent from the 15 raw features listed, but there is no stated exclusion rule.
Calibration and log_loss degrade with ratios, and a fixed 0.5 threshold gives low recall (about 0.21) in every stage. Any use of probabilities or a thresholded decision is unsupported.

The selection rule's tolerance (0.002) is much smaller than the fold std, so it cannot separate stages. The 'selected' stage (25 features, ROC-AUC 0.7029) does not match what the stated rule would pick (ratios). Its role and generation procedure are undocumented, and it performs worse than raw.
Default lightgbm hyperparameters were used for all stages. Extra features might change the optimal parameters, so the comparison may be tuned unfairly in either direction.
The limitations list in the evidence bundle is empty, although the claim itself lists a domain-semantics limitation. Dataset size, class balance and missing-value handling are not shown.

challenges_to_claims.issue: The question asks about 'strongest stable' evidence, but extra_trees has the second-highest fold std of five models (0.0295). Its win depends on the weak 0.25×std penalty and a ~0.008 score margin. The stability framing is unsupported.

3 folds × 1 repeat with no paired test. Per-fold advantage over logistic_regression and lightgbm changes sign, and the lead is driven largely by one fold, so the ranking is not demonstrated to be reproducible.
The comparison covers default-parameter baselines only. It cannot speak to algorithm families in general, only to these default implementations.
ROC-AUC-only selection ignores that logistic_regression is better on log_loss, brier, ece_10, accuracy and mean avg_precision. 'Candidate' status is metric-dependent and should be stated.
Unverified leakage and production-availability status of the 'ratios' features. The claim names the feature set without decision-time review, and top features include ratios of encoded categoricals.
The claim's 'ratios' feature set is not compared with the base feature set in this bundle, so the model candidate is conflated with feature-stage choice.

decision: Retain extra_trees only as a provisional training-CV leading candidate, with logistic_regression and lightgbm kept as live contenders. Do not call it the stable or best algorithm family. Do not approve any feature or model for deployment, and do not touch the locked holdout until the rank is confirmed under repeated paired CV and a decision-time/production-availability review of the features is done.

next_experiment.hypothesis: If extra_trees' ROC-AUC lead is real rather than fold noise, it will remain rank 1 on mean − 0.25×std over repeated stratified CV with identical splits for all models, and its paired ROC-AUC difference versus each of logistic_regression and lightgbm will be positive with an interval excluding zero.
next_experiment.success_gate: Using 5 repeats × 3 folds on the same training data (fixed seeds, all preprocessing and encoding fit inside each training fold, same ratios stage, default params), extra_trees ranks 1 by the EXP-009 selection rule, and the paired mean ROC-AUC difference versus both logistic_regression and lightgbm is > 0 with a repeated-CV-corrected 95% interval (e.g., Nadeau–Bengio) excluding 0. It is also reported with log_loss and ece_10 so that any calibration cost is visible. If the interval includes 0 or another model ranks 1, the 'extra_trees candidate' claim is falsified and the finding becomes 'no reliably separable leader'.
next_experiment.title: Repeated paired CV re-ranking of the five baselines on identical splits
next_experiment.why_smallest: It changes only the number of repeats and adds paired reporting. It reuses the existing five models, defaults and feature stage, with no tuning, no new features and no holdout access. It directly tests the weakest link, which is rank reproducibility. Documenting split type and the within-fold preprocessing check comes free with the rerun.

risks_and_missing_evidence: Only 3 folds and 1 repeat. The reported ci95 appears to be a normal-approximation interval (about ±1.96 SE) on 3 non-independent folds, so it understates uncertainty. It should not support rank claims.
No paired or significance comparison between models. Fold-level ROC-AUC ranges overlap heavily, and extra_trees' minimum fold (0.6948) is about equal to logistic_regression's minimum (0.6944).

All models use default parameters (model_params {}, optimization baseline), so the comparison may reflect defaults rather than family capability. Tuning could change the order, and nested CV would be needed to tune without optimistic bias.

Only the 'ratios' feature stage appears in the package. The claim says 'using ratios features', but there is no comparison against the raw/base stage. The utility of the ratio features is unestablished.

Many engineered features are ratios or log1p of categorical columns (job, month, day_of_week, poutcome, marital, loan). This implies integer or ordinal encodings, so the ratios are of arbitrary codes with questionable meaning. Encoding details are not shown.

Leakage risk is undocumented. It is unstated whether imputation, encoding or any target-based encoding was fit inside each training fold only. Whether a post-contact variable such as 'duration' was excluded is also unstated, since only the top-20 features are shown. Split type (stratified or not, shuffled or time-ordered) is not given.

Decision-time and production availability are unreviewed for the top features. poutcome, contact, pdays, previous, month and day_of_week reflect prior and current campaign contact context and need review. Timing of the day_of_week/month values relative to the prediction point must be confirmed.
Class prevalence and positive count per fold are not given. Recall values imply about 124–125 positives per fold (my inference), so the metrics are noisy.
Threshold fixed at 0.5 with low recall. There is no threshold, cost or utility analysis, and ROC-AUC alone is insufficient for any actionable use.
Calibration is worse for extra_trees than for logistic_regression and none of the models were calibrated. Probabilities from extra_trees should not be used as-is.
Feature importances come from different mechanisms per model and are missing for hist_gradient_boosting. Cross-model stability comparison is not valid, and importance is not causal.
Bundle-level limitations is empty, so caveats are under-reported.

challenges_to_claims.issue: The numbers match the evidence paths, but the claim has no limitations listed. The interval is wide, only holdout resampling variance is covered, and nothing connects the holdout result to the question about CV gain from optimization. It also does not show that the recipe was preselected independently of the holdout.
The bundle answers only the second half of the question. No evidence supports or refutes a meaningful optimization gain in CV.

The recommendation is sensible but unsupported by per-feature review. No feature has been checked for decision-time or production availability. Stability evidence (3 folds, impurity-style importance) is weak, and redundant or engineered features (log1p_*, ratio_*) dominate the list.
Feature importance must not be read as a causal or business driver. Importance of poutcome, month, etc. reflects predictive use in this model only.

decision: Do not claim a meaningful CV gain from optimization; the evidence is insufficient. Report the holdout ROC-AUC 0.7718 (interval 0.7126–0.8290) as a single, now-spent estimate with wide uncertainty. Do not approve any feature or the model for deployment. Treat C2 as a reasonable guardrail that has not yet been applied feature by feature.

next_experiment.hypothesis: On identical repeated stratified CV splits of the training data only, extra_trees_C02 improves mean ROC-AUC over baseline by at least 0.001, with a paired-difference interval excluding 0. Removing the log1p_* and ratio_* features derived from categorical or ordinal-coded columns does not reduce ROC-AUC by more than 0.001.
next_experiment.success_gate: Paired mean ΔAUC (C02 − baseline) ≥ 0.001 and the 95% interval of paired fold deltas (e.g. 5×3 or 5×5 repeated CV) has a lower bound > 0. For the ablation, the paired ΔAUC (reduced − full) is ≥ −0.001. If either condition fails, report that optimization or the engineered features show no demonstrated value, and prefer baseline or the simpler feature set. Use only training data, and confirm that all encoders and feature engineering are fit inside each fold.
next_experiment.title: Paired repeated-CV comparison of baseline vs extra_trees_C02, with and without engineered categorical transforms
next_experiment.why_smallest: It reuses the existing recipes and the training CV with no new data or holdout access. It directly answers the unanswered CV-gain question and tests the most suspicious feature-engineering choice, using one paired design and a pre-stated gate.

risks_and_missing_evidence: No baseline vs tuned CV mean/std, per-fold deltas, or candidate list, so the 0.001 gate cannot be verified. A 0.001 AUC threshold is likely within fold-to-fold noise.
It is unclear whether extra_trees_C02 was selected by the gate or is a tuned or fixed recipe. Preselection is asserted but not evidenced, and the holdout cannot be reused to check it.

Holdout size, positive count and prevalence are not given, so the interval width and the precision/recall figures cannot be interpreted. The bootstrap captures only test-sample variance, not training or seed variance.
The threshold of 0.5 is not justified. Recall of 0.138 indicates most positives are missed, and no cost or threshold analysis is provided.

Importance type is unspecified (probably impurity-based). It is biased toward high-cardinality or continuous features, and it splits across correlated features such as poutcome and log1p_poutcome. It is also computed on a single fit.
Engineered ratio and log features of categorical or ordinal codes may encode arbitrary label-encoding order. Their ratio_* items in the top 15 may reflect artifacts rather than signal.

Leakage review is absent. The bundle does not state whether known leaky fields (e.g. call duration in bank marketing) were excluded, nor whether encoders and engineered features were fit inside CV folds only.
Features such as poutcome, pdays, month, day_of_week and contact need decision-time and production-availability checks. None are documented here.
The 3-fold stability analysis is coarse. top10_frequency takes only four values, and the rank ordering is unstable beyond the top ~7 features.
Holdout is consumed, so any further tuning on it would be invalid. Further holdout-based claims need fresh data or a temporal split.
Claims C1 and C2 list empty limitations despite the issues above.

challenges_to_claims.issue: The numeric facts are traceable to evidence.source_rows, feature_count, and positive_rate_train. However, the claim omits the holdout size, the positive-class definition, and the split method, and its limitations list is empty despite the small sample.

'1 features triggered' is not verifiable because only 10 of 30 profiles are present. The wording also lumps four rule types together while the only visible trigger is random-split shift. The claim is framed as a production risk, but a random-split PSI cannot establish production instability. No threshold or null calibration is provided.
The categorical-factorization limitation does not obviously apply to the profiled float64 features, which suggests boilerplate caveats or an unexplained scope gap.

The package never addresses identifier or leakage review beyond unique_ratio and top_value_frequency. High unique_ratio on continuous floats is expected and is not a leakage test, and no decision-time availability check is present.

decision: Do not proceed to modeling or approve any feature yet. Treat EXP-011 as an incomplete data-understanding pass. First regenerate the full 30-feature profile, calibrate the PSI flag against a null distribution, and document the label definition, split design, and decision-time/production availability of each feature.

next_experiment.hypothesis: The fractal_dimension1 random-split PSI of about 0.218 is within sampling noise for this sample size. Under repeated stratified random splits of the same size, it will not exceed the 95th percentile of the null PSI distribution for that feature.
next_experiment.success_gate: Profile all 30 features, and for each compute the PSI null distribution over at least 200 seeded stratified random splits with the same train/holdout sizes. The hypothesis is falsified if the observed fractal_dimension1 PSI (about 0.218) exceeds the 95th percentile of its null, or if any other feature exceeds its own 95th percentile. In addition, the run must output the exact duplicate-row count, the label definition, the holdout size and positive rate, and a per-feature decision-time/availability annotation. Features without that annotation stay unapproved.
next_experiment.title: Full-feature profile with null-calibrated random-split PSI and a duplicate/group check
next_experiment.why_smallest: It reuses the existing profiling code and the cached matrix, with no model training. It adds only a full-feature pass, a repeated-split null, and metadata checks, and these resolve the unverifiable claim count, the uninterpretable PSI flag, and the missing availability review.

risks_and_missing_evidence: Only 10 of 30 feature profiles are present, so the claimed count of flagged features is unverifiable (EXP-011 / evidence.feature_count vs evidence.feature_profiles).

The PSI flag threshold, bin count, and train/holdout sizes are not recorded. Holdout positive rate and stratification are also unknown, so the 0.218 PSI cannot be interpreted (EXP-011 / evidence.feature_profiles; evidence.positive_rate_train).
The label definition and the meaning of the positive class are not documented.
No duplicate-row or repeated-subject/group check is reported. If one subject contributes multiple rows, random splitting could leak (EXP-011 / evidence.source_rows).
No decision-time or production-availability review exists for any feature, so no feature can be approved.
No correlation or redundancy analysis is given. Size-related features such as radius, perimeter, and area may be highly collinear (unverified).
Feature provenance (computation pipeline, whether derived from post-outcome or post-diagnostic steps) is undocumented.
Random-split PSI says nothing about temporal, site, or instrument drift (EXP-011 / claims[EXP-011-C2].limitations).
The factorized-categorical caveat is unexplained: no categorical features are evident in the shown profiles, so applicability is unclear.
Empty limitations on C1 and at bundle level understate uncertainty, for example small sample size (569 rows).

challenges_to_claims.issue: Factually supported, but it is a detector sanity check only. It shows the tool works on an exact-target canary, not that the breast_cancer columns are clean. The empty limitations field overstates its scope.

The claim 'Declared decision-time exclusions: none' is a decision resting on an empty declaration list and a null safe_vs_unsafe_training_cv. No decision-time semantics review is cited, and the claim risks being read as 'no leakage found'. It should be reworded as 'no exclusions declared; audit incomplete'.

decision: Do not treat 'none' as a clean audit result. Mark the leakage audit for breast_cancer as inconclusive pending per-column detector output, a documented decision-time and production-availability review, and a populated safe-vs-unsafe CV comparison. No features are approved.

next_experiment.hypothesis: If the detector and the column set are clean, then (a) the detector flags graded synthetic proxies (target plus noise at several levels) above a stated sensitivity threshold, (b) no real column exceeds the pre-registered univariate AUC and uniqueness thresholds without a documented decision-time justification, and (c) removing any flagged columns changes grouped-CV performance by less than a pre-registered margin.
next_experiment.success_gate: Before running, pre-register the AUC and uniqueness thresholds, the noise levels, and the CV margin. The gate passes only if: the detector flags every graded canary at or above the pre-registered detectability level; each real column has a recorded detector output plus a written decision-time and production-availability determination; and safe_vs_unsafe_training_cv is non-null with fold-level scores. Any real column over threshold without justification fails the gate and goes to semantic review rather than being auto-excluded or auto-approved.
next_experiment.title: Per-column leakage screen with a graded-proxy canary and a populated safe-vs-unsafe CV
next_experiment.why_smallest: It reuses the existing detector and canary, adds only graded-noise canaries and per-column logging, and fills the one null evidence field, with no new models or feature engineering.

risks_and_missing_evidence: safe_vs_unsafe_training_cv is null, so claim C2's cited evidence is missing and there is no measured effect of removing suspect columns.
No per-column audit output (name-pattern hits, univariate AUC, uniqueness or cardinality), so it is unknown which columns were screened and with what thresholds.
The canary tests only an exact-target copy; sensitivity to noisy, transformed, or partial proxies is untested, and no false-negative rate is given.
No decision-time or production-availability review is recorded for any column, which is required before any feature is approved.

Dataset provenance is unreviewed. For the breast_cancer diagnostic data, features are computed from cell-nucleus images; whether the same measurements exist at the actual prediction moment (e.g., before diagnosis or biopsy) is a semantic question the data cannot answer. Possible duplicate or near-duplicate rows and patient-level grouping are also unchecked.
No validation-design evidence (split strategy, grouping, preprocessing fit inside folds), so leakage via the validation pipeline cannot be excluded.
The limitations list is empty at bundle level even though C2 states limitations, which understates the uncertainty.

challenges_to_claims.issue: The claim reports a single-metric mean (0.9907) as if raw were superior, but full_fe, logs and the others are within noise of it. Raw is selected only by a parsimony tie-break, and the claim does not say so.
The evidence is training-CV only, with 3 folds and 1 repeat. There is no held-out confirmation and no paired uncertainty on stage differences.
The claim ignores that the ratios stage is better on log loss, Brier, ECE and accuracy. The metric choice is unjustified and can flip the recommendation.
It is not shown that engineered and selected features were fitted train-fold-only, and the selected stage's degradation is unexplained. A leakage or selection-procedure defect cannot be excluded.
The claim says 'about 30 features'. The evidence gives exactly 30.0, so this is only a minor precision issue. It also implies no dilution evaluation, which was not performed.

decision: Retain raw as the parsimonious baseline for the next LightGBM screen only. Do not state that feature engineering was shown not to help, and do not approve any engineered feature. No deployment approval. The ratio-based recipes remain open candidates because of their better calibration and threshold metrics.

next_experiment.hypothesis: Raw is non-inferior to ratios and full_fe on ROC-AUC (paired mean difference no worse than 0.002), and the ratios recipe gives a lower log loss than raw. The raw-vs-ratios results above are a candidate effect, not a finding.
next_experiment.success_gate: On identical stratified folds (for example 5x repeated 5-fold) with fixed LightGBM params, compute paired per-fold differences against raw. Raw is retained as the baseline if the lower 95% CI bound of (raw minus candidate) ROC-AUC is above -0.002 and the ratios log-loss improvement CI includes zero. The ratios recipe is promoted to the next screen only if its paired log-loss improvement has a 95% CI excluding zero and its ROC-AUC loss versus raw is within 0.002. All feature generation and selection must be shown to be fitted inside each training fold, and a held-out split must stay untouched for one final confirmation. Any promoted engineered feature still needs a decision-time and production-availability review by a domain expert.
next_experiment.title: Paired repeated-CV non-inferiority and calibration check of raw vs ratios vs full_fe
next_experiment.why_smallest: It reuses the three existing stages and the same model, and adds only repeats, shared folds, and paired statistics. It introduces no new features and no tuning, so it directly resolves the noise, metric-choice and fold-leakage ambiguities.

risks_and_missing_evidence: Only training-CV is reported. There is no held-out validation or test result, so 'validation evidence' in the question is not actually supplied, and selecting on CV then reporting CV is optimistic.

Fit-within-fold behavior is not documented. The bundle does not show that ratio, interaction, log, and selection steps were fitted inside each training fold. The selected stage always has exactly 25 features, which suggests a fixed k and needs a leakage check.

3 folds and 1 repeat give wide intervals, and the 0.002 tolerance is smaller than the fold std (about 0.0065). The rule can pick a winner among statistically tied options. No paired fold-wise comparison is provided.

Selection used ROC-AUC alone. Log loss, Brier, ECE, accuracy and F1 at a fixed 0.5 threshold favor the ratios stage over raw, and the ranking differs by metric. Whether ranking or calibration matters is not stated.
Feature dilution is not measured. There is no explicit dilution metric, and importance-based stability from 3 folds is weak evidence.
Logs results are identical to raw to full precision despite 24 extra features. This is unexplained and could be a pipeline artifact (features dropped, deduplicated, or never used).

Results are for one model with default parameters (model_params empty, baseline optimization). The recommendation to use raw does not transfer to linear or other models that benefit from log or ratio features.

Decision-time and production availability are not reviewed for any feature. Engineered features such as ratio_area3_div_area1 and ratio_area3_div_perimeter1 combine mean and worst-case measurements, and their meaning and availability at decision time are unchecked. Importance rankings are not causal.
Dataset size, class balance, stratification, and the split seed are not stated, so the CV design cannot be audited.

challenges_to_claims.issue: The claim's wording as the 'training-CV model candidate' is acceptable as a recommendation, but the evidence package does not show that logistic_regression is stably better than the alternatives. The ROC-AUC CIs overlap, there are 3 folds and 1 repeat, and there is one tie fold.
The comparison is among untuned baselines (optimization=baseline, model_params={}). It cannot support conclusions about the algorithm family, which the question asks.
Preprocessing, fold-internal fitting, stratification, and duplicate or group leakage are not documented. 'Raw features' is not sufficient to rule out leakage or an unfair setup.
No decision-time or production-availability review exists for the 30 input features. The claim must not be read as approving the feature set.
The bundle's top-level limitations list is empty, which understates the caveats the claim itself acknowledges.

decision: Keep logistic_regression as a provisional training-CV candidate only. Do not describe it as the strongest stable algorithm family or as a winner over the tree models. Do not approve deployment or any feature for use. The locked holdout stays untouched until a repeated-CV paired comparison supports or rejects the lead.

next_experiment.hypothesis: If logistic_regression is truly better than the tree and boosting baselines on ROC-AUC, it will beat the best-performing alternative on paired per-split differences in repeated CV. Otherwise the current lead is fold noise.
next_experiment.success_gate: Using the same stratified splits for all five models (e.g., 5-fold × 10 repeats, with all preprocessing fit inside training folds only, and with duplicate/group overlap checked first), logistic_regression keeps rank 1 under the existing selection rule. Its paired mean ROC-AUC difference vs the best alternative is greater than 0, with the 95% CI lower bound above 0. The gate fails if the CI includes 0 or any other model ranks first, in which case the claim is downgraded to 'no distinguishable leader'.
next_experiment.title: Repeated stratified paired CV on identical splits, defaults only
next_experiment.why_smallest: It adds no new models, tuning, features, or holdout access. It changes only the resampling design (more repeats on shared splits) and adds a paired analysis, which directly tests the one weakness in the ranking evidence: whether the margin exceeds fold noise.

risks_and_missing_evidence: Only 3 folds and 1 repeat. Fold std and the CI are estimated from n=3, so they are unreliable, and the 0.25×std penalty adds little discrimination.
No paired fold-difference analysis. It is not documented that all models used identical splits, so the pairing is unverified.
All models are baselines with empty model_params, so no tuning budget was spent on any family. The boosted and tree models could gain more from tuning than logistic_regression.

Preprocessing is undocumented for 'raw features': whether scaling or imputation is fit inside each training fold, and whether splits are stratified. Fold-external fitting would be a leakage risk, and unscaled logistic_regression would be a different model than assumed.
No check for duplicate or near-duplicate rows or grouped samples (e.g., multiple records per patient or source) across folds. Such overlap would inflate every model's CV score.

Decision-time and production-availability review of the 30 features (names like radius1, texture3, concave_points1) is absent. No feature is approved. Whether these measurements exist at the intended prediction time is unverified.

ROC-AUC is near its ceiling (about 0.99). The metric is insensitive for separating the models, and the threshold is fixed at 0.5 with no cost-based review. Recall differs across models (0.91 to 0.96) but fold counts are small, so errors per fold are few and noisy.
ece_10 on small folds with 10 bins is noisy and should not be used to claim better calibration.

Importance method is unspecified, and hist_gradient_boosting has no stability output. Features such as radius, perimeter, and area are likely correlated, so importance rankings can be unstable and cannot support causal or mechanistic statements.
One dataset only, so the question's phrase 'for this dataset profile' cannot be generalized beyond breast_cancer. The locked holdout has not been used.

challenges_to_claims.issue: The numbers match the evidence. The claim does not address the CV-gain question, omits the missing CV comparison, and has empty limitations. Its interval is holdout-resampling only and is capped at 1.0, and the holdout size is unreported. 'Preselected' is asserted without provenance.

The recommendation is reasonable, but the cited evidence is only a 3-fold importance ranking with an unspecified method and no availability or monitoring data. It cannot support promoting or demoting any specific feature. Importance must not be read causally, and collinearity can distort it. Empty limitations understate this.

decision: Record C1 as a descriptive holdout observation only. Do not claim that optimization did or did not yield a meaningful CV gain until CV evidence is supplied. Keep C2 as a recommendation, since it is a governance rule rather than an empirical finding. Approve no feature and no deployment. The holdout is consumed, so it must not be used for further selection or tuning.

next_experiment.hypothesis: The best tuned candidate's mean ROC-AUC improvement over baseline is no larger than CV noise, so retaining baseline is justified. This is falsified if the improvement is both at least 0.001 and consistently positive across repeated paired folds.
next_experiment.success_gate: Run repeated stratified CV (for example 5 repeats x 5 folds, identical splits for all candidates, training data only, holdout untouched). Report fold-level paired ROC-AUC differences (tuned minus baseline) with a CI. Reject the 'no meaningful gain' hypothesis only if the mean paired difference is at least 0.001 and the 95% CI of the paired difference excludes 0. Otherwise confirm baseline. Also report the SD of paired differences to show the 0.001 gate against noise.
next_experiment.title: Repeated paired CV audit of the tuned-vs-baseline gain (training data only)
next_experiment.why_smallest: It reuses the existing candidates and selection rule, needs no new model families, features or holdout access, and directly answers the unanswered CV-gain question with a paired, falsifiable comparison.

risks_and_missing_evidence: No per-candidate CV ROC-AUC, baseline CV ROC-AUC, fold-level scores, or paired deltas are provided, so the main question is unanswered and the 0.001 selection gate cannot be audited.
The 0.001 threshold is not compared with fold-to-fold noise. With 3-fold CV the gate may be well inside noise.
No evidence shows the recipe was fixed before the holdout was evaluated (no timestamp or preregistration path), although the claim says 'preselected'.

The holdout size and class counts are not reported. Precision 0.975 and recall 0.9286 are consistent with a small holdout of roughly 114 rows (inference), so a few errors move the metrics substantially.
The bootstrap resamples only the holdout, with 400 draws. It does not capture split-to-split or training variability, and the upper bound of 1.0 is a ceiling artifact.

Holdout accuracy, precision, recall and calibration (ECE 0.030) are reported only at the 0.5 threshold. The positive class and the error costs are not stated, so the recall of 0.9286 cannot be judged clinically or operationally.

The importance method for 'normalized_importance' is unspecified (coefficient magnitude, permutation, or other). It is unclear whether the importances come from the logistic model or from a different model.
Collinear features (radius/perimeter/area groups) can make per-feature importance and top-10 frequency unstable. Grouped or permutation importance has not been checked.

No decision-time availability or production-availability review is documented for any feature. The WDBC-style features derive from image measurements, and their timing and pipeline dependencies are unknown.
The result comes from a single small public benchmark (breast_cancer), so it gives no evidence of external or temporal generalization.
The limitations fields are empty even though the issues above exist.

challenges_to_claims.issue: The numbers are supported by the evidence paths, but the claim has no limitations and omits split sizes and holdout class balance. With only 303 rows, any later performance estimate will be high variance. It also says '13 cached features' while only 10 are profiled.

The claim lumps four rule types (missingness, identifier, near-constant, shift) into a count of 3, but the visible evidence shows only shift flags. The evidence path points to the whole feature_profiles array and covers only 10 of 13 features, so the count cannot be verified for the full feature set. The shift flags rest on a random-split PSI that is likely noise-dominated and computed on factorized codes. The claim also does not address production availability, which the question asks about.
The 0.0 missing_rate on every visible feature is not discussed in the claim, yet it is the only evidence on missingness and the upstream factorization limitation undermines it.

decision: Do not proceed to modeling or approve any feature. Treat this as an incomplete data-understanding result. Complete the profile for all 13 features, restore raw categorical and missing-value semantics, calibrate the PSI screen, and document a decision time and per-feature production availability before any modeling.

next_experiment.hypothesis: The split_distribution_shift flags on age, trestbps and chol are artifacts of small-holdout sampling noise or binning, not real distribution differences. If so, their observed PSI will fall within the null PSI distribution from repeated random stratified splits.

(2) PSI binning and threshold are documented. (3) Over at least 500 seeded stratified random splits with the same train and holdout sizes, the per-feature null PSI 95th percentile is reported. The hypothesis is falsified for a feature if its observed PSI exceeds that feature's null 95th percentile, in which case split or binning logic must be investigated. It is supported if all three observed PSIs fall at or below their null 95th percentiles. (4) A decision time and a per-feature source and availability table exist and are reviewed. It requires no model training and resolves the largest uncertainties, which are profile completeness, missingness validity and whether the shift flags are noise.

risks_and_missing_evidence: Profiles are missing for 3 of 13 declared features, so quality and shift flags are unassessed for them. Their names are not given in the package.

missing_rate 0.0 on all profiled features may reflect upstream factorization or imputation rather than true completeness. Raw missing codes are not shown and original UCI missingness cannot be ruled out.

Categoricals (sex, cp, fbs, restecg, exang) are stored as int64 factorized codes. Numeric treatment, PSI and ordering on these codes may be semantically meaningless, and the production encoder mapping is unknown.

PSI details are undocumented: binning scheme, flag threshold (visible flags only at 0.2776 and above, none at 0.1935 and below) and the reason PSI is null for some features but not others. The age PSI of 0.746 under a random split is unexplained.
